what.text: By the end of 2025, there were 174607 refugees from Western Sahara living across all host countries combined.
The main country of asylum was Algeria with 173600 refugees at year end, while others resided in France, Cuba, Angola, and Venezuela.

why.text: The provided sources do not detail the causes of displacement from Western Sahara.
No specific events, active conflicts, or opposition groups are recorded in the fact pack.

when.text: In 1975, the year-end refugee total for Western Sahara was recorded at 20000.
Data notes highlight big changes between 1975 and 1976 and between 1980 and 1981, followed by very slow, steady change from 1981 to 2004.
After another big change between 2023 and 2024, the count reached 174607 by the end of 2025.

how.text: The sources don't say what travel routes people used or how they live in host countries.
Refugees and asylum seekers are counted as year-end totals on 31 December in all host countries combined under UNHCR's mandate.
Refugee returns represent a yearly count of refugees returning to Western Sahara from all host countries during each year.
